To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the RGD peptide-fusing recombinant mussed adhesive protein was successfully introduced to the silkworm silk fiber, which resulted in the improved adhesion and proliferation of mammalian cells.

we improved the overall properties of silkworm SF by introducing RGD-biofunctionalized recombinant MAP and demonstrated that the MAP-RGD blended SF fibers could be used for various biomedical applications, including biomolecule immobilization, cell attachment, and tissue regeneration.

the MAP-RGD blended SF material has improved adhesion, proliferation and spreading of mammal cells, and enhanced attachment of biomolecules including carbohydrate and protein, without hampering the original mechanical properties and biodegradibility of SF.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a simple and versatile approach for the preparation of a multifunctional silk-based material with excellent adhesive properties.
a novel approach for improving the overall characteristics of silk fibroin.
a novel approach to the development of a multifunctional biomaterial for biomedical applications.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this work provides an efficient approach to improve the adhesive and biological properties of SF by blending with MAP-RGD.
this material could be used for various biomedical applications, such as wound healing and tissue engineering, as well as for cell and protein immobilization.
this study has demonstrated that the simple blending of MAP-RGDS could provide the SF material with multifunctional properties such as adhesion, cell attachment, and biodegradation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the RGD-bioactive MAP-blended SF material could be used in various biomedical engineering applications.
the MAP-RGD fusion protein could be a good candidate to improve the adhesive ability of silk.
MAP-RGD-blending is a promising strategy to enhance the biological functions and biodegradabilty of SF.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the simple blending of MAP-RG with SF can provide a multifunctional silk-based biomaterial for various applications.
the simple blending of MAP-RGDbioconjugated protein can provide not only bulk-scale but also microscale adhesive ability to silk fibroin.
the blending of RGD-conjugated MAP into SF can provide the material with both adhesive and biological functionalities.
